A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuroAdapter and IBBI work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, figures, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon, together with model ablations, attention visualizations, and ROI-masking results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds candidate-selection controls, denoising-step experiments, and quantitative evaluation of IBBI attention maps.

M1.justification: The architecture, parcel conditioning, training loss, attention aggregation, and encoder-based image selection remain unchanged. Section 3.3 changes token-retention probability from r to 1-r, but r is uniformly sampled on (0,1) in both versions, making the masking distributions equivalent. The added mask processing serves evaluation rather than changing the decoder.

E1.justification: Both versions use NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon with the same perception, imagery, natural-image, and artificial-shape coverage. The new attention-overlap analysis quantitatively evaluates the existing Face, Body, Scene, and Word localization analysis on reconstructed images; it introduces no new data domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds Lowest-Corr and Random selection controls alongside Highest-Corr selection in Table 11, and a whole-image-mask baseline for IBBI in Table 13. SAM3 supplies reference masks rather than serving as a competing decoder. Existing reconstruction comparator sets, including MindEye2 in Table 3, are retained.

E3.justification: Original benchmark settings remain unchanged. Added protocols compare three selection rules over eight candidates, sweep denoising steps from 20 to 80, and evaluate attention masks using IoU and Dice against SAM3 masks. Appendix O specifies temporal averaging, normalization, a 50% threshold, and 236 valid images among 515 reconstructions.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends validation with selection controls in Appendix K, denoising-step sensitivity in Appendix L, and quantitative semantic-localization analysis in Appendix O. The latter directly tests spatial specificity previously illustrated through attention visualizations. Existing dropout, dimensionality, parcel-count, mapping, candidate-count, and ROI-masking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already generate candidates using different random seeds and evaluate candidate counts up to eight. The added selection experiment uses this existing sampling practice. v2 introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, repeated-training-run uncertainty, or other new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 11–13 add substantial evidence about selection, denoising sensitivity, and attention localization. For example, Table 13 reports Face IoU of 0.322 for IBBI versus 0.124 for the whole-image baseline, but Scene IoU of 0.198 versus 0.605. All numerical entries in v1 Tables 1–10 and its ROI-masking Table 11, now Table 14, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 retains the same cross-attention, parcel-contribution, and ROI-map definitions. The min-SNR equations move from Appendix L to Appendix M without substantive revision. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced; IoU and Dice are added as empirical evaluation metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and discussion retain the same central claims: direct parcel-based diffusion conditioning, competitive reconstruction without intermediate embedding alignment, and bidirectional attention-based interpretability. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets encoder selection as prioritizing neural fidelity while acknowledging that random candidates sometimes score better perceptually. It also interprets denoising-step stability and explains weaker Scene overlap through broad SAM3 background masks versus selective IBBI attention. These add substantive qualifications to otherwise retained interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: v1 promises code after acceptance; v2 provides project and repository links and states that code and reproduction instructions are available. Appendix O additionally documents attention-mask processing. Reported hardware, 300 training epochs, batch size 16, and approximately 25-hour training time are unchanged. Repository contents were not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through explicit comparison with single-stage Dynadiff, functional-alignment work, interpretable encoders, and language-neuroscience approaches. Section 3.4 newly credits Kneeland et al. for encoder-based selection. The Deeprecon novelty statement narrows from modern decoding models to diffusion-based pipelines. The MindEye2 reference is removed, although its evaluated results remain.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites and expands related work, polishes the abstract and several explanatory passages, adds acknowledgments, and updates publication headers and terminology. New appendix sections are integrated through renumbering. The principal section sequence and most method and experimental exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–13 and a segmentation-comparison Figure 13, expands Figures 6–7 captions, and adjusts table formatting and figure placement. Existing ROI-masking displays and subsequent figures are renumbered. The original reconstruction images, attention panels, and comparison plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing work through quantitative attention-map validation, better selection controls, denoising sensitivity checks, clearer research positioning, and explicit code-access information. These provide useful support beyond v1’s existing benchmarks and ROI-masking evidence. The gain remains bounded: localization uses SAM3 pseudo-labels, includes only seven Word examples, and lacks uncertainty estimates, while the original reconstruction results remain unchanged.
